evals.prompt: We want to post a Slack message whenever a review run finishes (server/src/modules/reviews). Where does the Slack integration code go, and can you sketch out the files I need?
evals.expected_output: Walks through the 5-step new-integration workflow: a Notifier-style port (in @devdigest/shared or a local types.ts), a concrete adapters/slack/*.ts implementation, a mock counterpart in adapters/mocks.ts, a lazy getter wired into platform/container.ts, and ReviewService/run-executor.ts consuming the port type via the container rather than importing the Slack adapter directly. Should NOT suggest importing the Slack client straight into the service or route.

assertions.text: Proposes defining a port/interface (e.g. Notifier) rather than referring to the Slack SDK type directly in service code
Places the concrete Slack implementation under adapters/<kind>/ (e.g. adapters/slack/*.ts)
Mentions adding a mock implementation (adapters/mocks.ts or module-local) so tests don't hit the real Slack API
Mentions wiring the new adapter into platform/container.ts (lazy getter / ContainerOverrides pattern)
Does not tell the user to import the Slack adapter class directly into service.ts instead of going through the container

evals.expected_output: Flags the direct adapter import/instantiation inside routes.ts as a layering violation, explains routes should only call a service method, and shows the fix: move the GitHub call into PullsService (or similar), which reads the client via container.github, with the route reduced to zod-validated params -> service call -> response mapping.

assertions.text: Explicitly identifies importing/instantiating the adapter directly inside routes.ts as a layering/architecture problem, not just a style nit
Proposes moving the GitHub call into a service method (e.g. on PullsService) instead of the route
Suggests obtaining the client via container.github (or an equivalent container-resolved interface) instead of `new OctokitGitHubClient(...)`
Describes or shows the resulting route reduced to param handling + service call + response mapping, with no adapter import left in routes.ts

evals.prompt: I'm adding logic to server/src/modules/pulls that recomputes a PR's diff stats (files changed, additions, deletions) from the stored diff blob whenever someone re-opens the PR detail page. Should this go in service.ts or repository.ts, and does reviewer-core need to know about it?
evals.expected_output: Places the pure diff-stat computation in service.ts (or a small domain helper) since it's a transformation with no I/O, keeps repository.ts limited to Drizzle read/write of the stored diff blob, and notes it does NOT belong in reviewer-core unless it becomes part of the shared diff->prompt->grounding pipeline — reviewer-core stays reserved for the actual review engine, not incidental PR-detail computations.

assertions.text: Recommends putting the diff-stat computation in service.ts (or a domain helper it calls), not repository.ts
States or implies repository.ts should stay limited to reading/writing the stored diff blob via Drizzle, not doing the computation
Explicitly says this does NOT belong in reviewer-core / reviewer-core does not need to know about it, since it's incidental to the review pipeline
